1	# Evaluate — Design and run Flow evaluations
2	
3	Capability index for `uip maestro flow eval` — evaluator CRUD (7 types), eval set CRUD with entry-point pinning, data point management with file attachments, and Studio Web run start/status/results/list/compare. Local CRUD is offline; runs require `uip login` and a Flow solution that already exists in Studio Web.
4	
5	> **Where you came from / where to go next.** Evaluate is downstream of Operate (ship the flow → evaluate it on Studio Web) and feeds back into Author (failing eval → fix the `.flow` → re-ship → re-evaluate). Build/edit lives in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md); publish/deploy lives in [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../operate/CAPABILITY.md); fault triage on a debug or process run lives in [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
6	>
7	> **Inherits universal rules from [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md)** — `--output json` + prefer `--output-filter` for extraction, no `flow debug` without consent, never invoke other skills automatically, dropdown question pattern, **plain-English narration + granular progress list (opt-in — silent by default; engage when the user asks for verbosity)**. The rules below are evaluate-scoped and apply on top.
8	
9	## When to use this capability
10	
11	- Add or remove data points (test cases) on a Flow eval set
12	- Create evaluators (`exact-match`, `json-similarity`, `contains`, `llm-judge-*` types) for a Flow project
13	- Create or remove eval sets, link them to evaluators, pin entry points
14	- Add, list, or remove simulations on data points (`uip maestro flow eval simulation`)
15	- Start an eval run on Studio Web, poll its status, fetch detailed results
16	- Compare two eval runs to verify a change improved scores without regressions
17	
18	For agent (`agent.json`) evaluations read the `uipath-agents` skill. For BPMN evaluations read the `uipath-maestro-bpmn` skill — this capability covers Flow only.
19	
20	## Critical rules
21	
22	1. **Check Flow eval CLI availability once.** Run `uip maestro flow eval --help --output json` before using eval commands. If it returns `unknown command 'eval'`, the installed CLI does not expose Flow eval yet. Stop, report that the user needs a CLI/tool version with Flow eval support, and do not spend turns searching npm packages or source bundles.
23	2. **Never run `uip solution upload` automatically as part of an eval workflow.** The eval run requires the Flow solution to already exist in Studio Web, but uploading from the local working tree clobbers whatever is on Studio Web. If the project was pulled from Studio Web (`uip solution download`), edited locally in VS Code, or scaffolded on disk and never uploaded, an unprompted upload will overwrite or push unintended state. Ask the user explicitly before any `uip solution upload` — see [upload-safety.md](references/upload-safety.md).
24	3. **`--path` accepts a Flow project directory OR a solution directory containing exactly one Flow project.** If the solution holds multiple Flow projects, point `--path` at the specific project directory.
25	4. **Local CRUD does not require login.** `add`, `remove`, `list` (data points / eval sets / evaluators) edit JSON on disk. Only `uip maestro flow eval run *` requires `uip login` and an existing Studio Web solution.
26	5. **Pin a model on every LLM-judge evaluator.** Empty/missing `model` produces a cryptic 500 from the LLM gateway after retries. Pass `--model <name>` on `evaluator add` or set `model` in the JSON.
27	6. **Declare input variables before adding data points with `--inputs`.** `eval add` validates input keys against the Flow's declared input variables and fails fast on unknown keys. Add missing input variables first (for example, `uip maestro flow variable add My.flow name --direction in --type string --output json`) or change the data point input JSON to match the Flow schema.
28	7. **Let the CLI manage evaluator references.** Eval sets store `evaluatorRefs` as the evaluator file refs produced by `evaluator add` (for example, `greeting-match-1234abcd.json`). If the set should use every evaluator that already exists, omit `--evaluators` so the CLI writes those generated file refs. If you must pass `--evaluators`, pass the evaluator id or generated file base/ref from `evaluator add/list` — never the display name alone (`greeting-match`), because Studio Web does not resolve display-name refs.
29	8. **Pre-empt timeouts on `run start --wait`.** The CLI blocks until the run reaches a terminal state or `--timeout` elapses. `--timeout` only stops local blocking — the run continues server-side; query progress with `eval run status <run_id>`.
30	
31	## Quick Start
32	
33	Standard workflow: scaffold evaluators → create eval set → add data points → confirm project is in Studio Web → run.
34	
35	```bash
36	# 1. Add an evaluator (local; no login required)
37	uip maestro flow eval evaluator add greeting-quality \
38	  --type llm-judge-output \
39	  --model gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 \
40	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
41	
42	# 2. Create an eval set, pin the entry point, and let the CLI attach
43	#    all current evaluators by generated file ref
44	uip maestro flow eval set add "Smoke Tests" \
45	  --entry-point /Main.bpmn#start \
46	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
47	
48	# 3. Add data points (test cases)
49	#    The `message` key must already be declared as a Flow input variable.
50	uip maestro flow eval add hello-test \
51	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
52	  --inputs '{"message":"hello"}' \
53	  --expected '{"reply":"Hello! How can I help you?"}' \
54	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
55	
56	# 4. Confirm the solution is in Studio Web
57	#    DO NOT auto-run `uip solution upload`. Ask the user. See upload-safety.md.
58	
59	# 5. Start the run and wait
60	uip maestro flow eval run start \
61	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
62	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow \
63	  --wait --timeout 600 --output json
64	
65	# 6. Inspect failures
66	uip maestro flow eval run results <eval_set_run_id> \
67	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
68	  --only-failed --verbose \
69	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
70	```

101	
102	- **Don't auto-run `uip solution upload`.** Even when an eval run errors with "solution not found in Studio Web", stop and ask the user — see [upload-safety.md](references/upload-safety.md). The local project may be ahead of, or diverged from, Studio Web.

104	- **Don't pass `--type` in PascalCase.** Only kebab-case is accepted: `exact-match`, `json-similarity`, `contains`, `llm-judge-output`, `llm-judge-strict-json`, `llm-judge-trajectory`, `llm-judge-trajectory-simulation`.

106	- **Don't compare runs from different eval sets.** `eval run compare` aligns by data-point name within the set; cross-set deltas are meaningless.
107	- **Don't omit `--model` on LLM-judge evaluators.** The cloud worker fail-fasts before calling the LLM gateway.
108	- **Don't run evals during `flow debug`.** `debug` is a separate Studio Web session; evals run against the deployed/published solution. Mixing them produces confusing run IDs.

1	# `uip maestro flow eval` Command Reference
2	
3	Complete syntax reference for every subcommand under `uip maestro flow eval`. All commands accept the global flags `--output <table|json|yaml|plain>` (default `json`), `--output-filter <jmespath>`, `--log-level <debug|info|warn|error>`, and `--log-file <path>`. Repeated reminders below: always pass `--output json` when an agent will parse the result.
4	
5	## Command Tree
6	
7	```
8	uip maestro flow eval
9	├── add        — Add a data point to an evaluation set
10	├── list       — List data points in an evaluation set
11	├── remove     — Remove a data point from an evaluation set
12	├── set
13	│   ├── add    — Create an evaluation set
14	│   ├── list   — List evaluation sets
15	│   └── remove — Remove an evaluation set
16	├── evaluator
17	│   ├── add    — Add an evaluator to the flow project
18	│   ├── list   — List evaluators in a flow project
19	│   └── remove — Remove an evaluator from a flow project
20	├── simulation
21	│   ├── add    — Add or update a simulation on a data point
22	│   ├── list   — List simulations on a data point
23	│   └── remove — Remove a simulation from a data point
24	└── run
25	    ├── start    — Start a Studio Web evaluation run
26	    ├── status   — Check the status of a run
27	    ├── results  — Get detailed per-data-point results
28	    ├── list     — List runs for an eval set
29	    └── compare  — Compare two runs side-by-side
30	```
31	
32	`add` / `remove` / `list` at the top level operate on **data points** (test cases) inside an eval set. Data points are stored inline within the eval set JSON, not as separate files.
33	
34	## Common Options
35	
36	Every subcommand accepts:
37	
38	| Flag | Required | Description |
39	|------|----------|-------------|
40	| `--path <path>` | No (defaults to `.`) | Flow project directory, or a solution directory containing exactly one Flow project |
41	| `--output <fmt>` | No (default `json`) | `table`, `json`, `yaml`, or `plain` |
42	| `--output-filter <expr>` | No | JMESPath expression applied to JSON output before printing |
43	
44	## Data Points (Test Cases)
45	
46	### `uip maestro flow eval add <name>`
47	
48	Add a data point to an eval set.
49	
50	| Flag | Required | Description |
51	|------|----------|-------------|
52	| `--set <name>` | Yes | Eval set name or ID |
53	| `--inputs <json>` | No | Input values as a JSON object; keys must be declared as Flow input variables |

132	
133	Simulations intercept specific nodes (connectors, agents, sub-flows) during an eval run and replace their real execution with a controlled response. Each simulation targets a single component by its `componentId` and applies one of three strategies.

135	### `uip maestro flow eval simulation add <component-id>`
136	
137	Add or replace a simulation on a data point. If a simulation for `<component-id>` already exists on the data point it is overwritten.
138	
139	| Flag | Required | Description |
140	|------|----------|-------------|
141	| `--set <name>` | Yes | Eval set name or ID |
142	| `--data-point <id>` | Yes | Data point name or ID |
143	| `--strategy <strategy>` | Yes | `Llm` or `Static` |
144	| `--component-type <type>` | Yes | Component type (e.g. `connector`, `agent`, `subflow`) |
145	| `--component-description <text>` | No | Human-readable label for the component |
146	| `--simulation-instructions <text>` | No | LLM prompt describing what the component should return (for `Llm` strategy) |
147	| `--mock-value <json>` | No | Static JSON output (for `Static` strategy) |
148	| `--output-schema <json>` | No | JSON Schema describing the expected output shape; passed to the LLM to constrain its response. **Auto-resolved from the `.flow` file when omitted for `Llm` strategy** — fails if the node is not found or has no outputs. Pass explicitly to override. |
149	| `--path <path>` | No | (see Common Options) |
150	
151	**Strategy guide:**
152	
153	| Strategy | When to use | Key flags |
154	|----------|-------------|-----------|
155	| `Llm` | Output should be realistic but non-deterministic | `--simulation-instructions`, `--output-schema` (auto-resolved) |
156	| `Static` | Output is fixed and deterministic | `--mock-value` |

158	**`--output-schema` auto-resolution for Llm simulations:** When omitted, the CLI reads the `.flow` file, finds the node by `<component-id>`, and derives the schema from the node's output definition (connector `outputJsonSchema`, agent `agentOutputVariables`, or `node.outputs`). The JSON Schema is sent alongside `--simulation-instructions` to the LLM, telling it what shape the output must conform to. Without it the LLM generates free-form text. For a connector that returns `{ status, message }` you would pass:
159	
160	```bash
161	--output-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string"},"message":{"type":"string"}}}'
162	```

170	  --strategy Llm \
171	  --component-type connector \

185	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json

1	# Eval Sets and Data Points
2	
3	An eval set is a JSON file that bundles test cases (data points) with the evaluators that score them. Each Flow project can have multiple eval sets — typically one per scenario (smoke, regression, edge cases).
4	
5	## Eval Set Lifecycle
6	
7	```bash
8	# Create
9	uip maestro flow eval set add "<set_name>" \
10	  [--evaluators <ref1>,<ref2>] \
11	  [--entry-point <node_id>] \
12	  --path <flow_project> --output json
13	
14	# List
15	uip maestro flow eval set list --path <flow_project> --output json
16	
17	# Remove
18	uip maestro flow eval set remove "<id_or_name>" --path <flow_project> --output json
19	```
20	
21	### `--evaluators`
22	
23	Comma-separated list of evaluator IDs or generated file base names. When omitted, the new eval set links to **all evaluators** present in the project at creation time and writes the generated evaluator file refs (for example, `greeting-match-62c0793a.json`). Prefer omission when the eval set should use every current evaluator.
24	
25	Do **not** pass an evaluator display name such as `greeting-match` to `--evaluators`; that writes the display name into `evaluatorRefs`, and Studio Web eval runs will not resolve it. If you need an explicit list, get the generated id/file ref from `uip maestro flow eval evaluator add/list --output json` and pass that value instead.
26	
27	Subsequent evaluators added to the project do NOT auto-attach — link them by re-running `set add` with explicit generated refs, or carefully repair the eval set's `evaluatorRefs` array using the evaluator file refs the CLI created.
28	
29	### `--entry-point`
30	
31	Stored as `selectedEntrypoint` on the eval set. Accepts either:
32	
33	- A flow path: `/Main.bpmn#start`
34	- A start node ID: `start_a1b2c3d4`
35	
36	The eval set's entry point is used by `eval run start` unless `--entry-point` is overridden at run time. Pin one explicitly when the flow has multiple entry points; otherwise the first start node found is used and may not be the one you intend.
37	
38	## Data Point Lifecycle
39	
40	Data points (test cases) live **inline** inside the eval set JSON, not as separate files. CRUD via `uip maestro flow eval add/list/remove`:
41	
42	```bash
43	# Add a data point
44	uip maestro flow eval add "<data_point_name>" \
45	  --set "<set_name>" \
46	  --inputs '{"...":"..."}' \
47	  [--expected '{"...":"..."}'] \
48	  [--criteria '{"<evaluator_id>": {...}}'] \
49	  [--input-file <key>=<path>] \
50	  [--search-text "<text>"] \
51	  --path <flow_project> --output json
52	
53	# List
54	uip maestro flow eval list --set "<set_name>" --path <flow_project> --output json
55	
56	# Remove
57	uip maestro flow eval remove "<id_or_name>" --set "<set_name>" --path <flow_project> --output json
58	```
59	
60	### `--inputs`
61	
62	JSON object whose keys must match the flow's declared input variables for the chosen entry point. `eval add` validates these keys and fails fast when an input key is not declared in the `.flow` file. Add missing variables first, or change the data point input JSON to match the Flow schema.
63	
64	For a simple string input named `name`:
65	
66	```bash
67	uip maestro flow variable add ./MySolution/MyFlow/MyFlow.flow name \
68	  --direction in --type string --output json
69	```
70	
71	### `--expected`
72	
73	JSON object representing the expected output. How it is consumed depends on the evaluator type:
74	
75	| Evaluator type | Reads `--expected` how |
76	|----------------|-----------------------|
77	| `exact-match` | Compares the output against `expected` verbatim (or `expected[targetKey]` if `--target-key` is set on the evaluator) |
78	| `json-similarity` | Tree-compared with tolerance |
79	| `contains` | Not used directly — see `--search-text` |
80	| `llm-judge-output` | Substituted into `{{ExpectedOutput}}` |
81	| `llm-judge-strict-json` | Substituted per-key into `{{ExpectedOutput}}` |
82	| `llm-judge-trajectory` | Used along with `--expected-agent-behavior` (set via `--criteria`) |
83	| `llm-judge-trajectory-simulation` | Same as `trajectory` plus simulation context |
84	
85	### `--criteria`
86	
87	Per-evaluator overrides keyed by evaluator ID. Use this when one eval set contains multiple evaluators and you want each to score against different criteria for the same data point. Most common shape:
88	
89	```json
90	{
91	  "<evaluator_ref_for_trajectory>": {
92	    "expectedAgentBehavior": "Agent calls the weather tool with the user's location, then returns a one-sentence summary."
93	  },
94	  "<evaluator_ref_for_output>": {
95	    "expectedOutput": {"summary": "Sunny in NYC, 72°F"}
96	  }
97	}
98	```
99	
100	If `--criteria` is omitted, evaluators fall back to `--expected` (for output evaluators) and to defaults (for trajectory evaluators). Always pass an explicit `expectedAgentBehavior` for trajectory evaluators — the LLM's score against an empty `{{ExpectedAgentBehavior}}` is meaningless.
101	
102	### `--input-file <key>=<path>`
103	
104	Repeatable. Attach a file as input under the given key. The CLI stages the file alongside the eval set so the runtime can read it during evaluation. Useful when the flow accepts file inputs (PDFs, CSVs, images) rather than JSON only.
105	
106	```bash
107	uip maestro flow eval add invoice-test \
108	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
109	  --inputs '{"orderId":"ORD-123"}' \
110	  --input-file invoice=./fixtures/invoice-123.pdf \
111	  --input-file receipt=./fixtures/receipt-123.png \
112	  --expected '{"total": 142.50}' \
113	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
114	```
115	
116	The file content is referenced from the eval set; do not delete the source file before the run completes.
117	
118	### `--search-text`
119	
120	Convenience flag for `contains` evaluators only. Attaches the search string to the data point so the contains evaluator knows what substring to test for. Equivalent to writing `criteria` for the contains evaluator.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow eval add success-keyword \
124	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
125	  --inputs '{"task":"deploy"}' \
126	  --search-text "deployment succeeded" \
127	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
128	```
129	
130	## Eval Set JSON Shape
131	
132	A typical eval set JSON file (created by `set add`):
133	
134	```json
135	{
136	  "id": "<uuid>",
137	  "name": "Smoke Tests",
138	  "version": "1.0",
139	  "evaluatorRefs": ["<evaluator-file-ref-1>.json", "<evaluator-file-ref-2>.json"],
140	  "selectedEntrypoint": "/Main.bpmn#start",
141	  "evaluations": [
142	    {
143	      "id": "<uuid>",
144	      "name": "hello-test",
145	      "inputs": {"message": "hello"},
146	      "expectedOutput": {"reply": "Hello! How can I help you?"},
147	      "evaluationCriterias": {
148	        "<evaluator-ref-2>": {
149	          "expectedAgentBehavior": "Agent responds with a friendly greeting."
150	        }
151	      }
152	    }
153	  ]
154	}
155	```
156	
157	Key fields:
158	
159	- `version: "1.0"` distinguishes the new eval format from any legacy variants. Keep this. <!-- version-check-skip --> (eval-set file schema version, CLI-emitted by `eval set add` — not a `.flow` version)
160	- `evaluatorRefs` references evaluator files generated by the CLI. Prefer CLI commands over hand-editing these refs.
161	- `selectedEntrypoint` is the eval set's pinned entry point. Override per-run with `eval run start --entry-point`.
162	- `evaluations[]` is the inline list of data points. Order is informational, not significant.
163	- `evaluationCriterias` (note plural) is the per-data-point per-evaluator override map.
164	
165	## Aligning Inputs with the Flow Schema
166	
167	The data point's `inputs` JSON must match the flow's input schema at the chosen entry point. Mismatches produce `eval add` errors such as `Input "name" is not declared as an input variable in the flow`. Two ways to verify before adding data points:
168	
169	1. Inspect `<flow>.flow` in the project for `variables` entries with `direction: "in"`.
170	2. Run `uip maestro flow variable list <flow_file> --output json`.
171	
172	## Simulations on Data Points
173	
174	Simulations replace selected nodes during an eval run with controlled outputs, so the flow is evaluated without calling real external services. Each simulation targets one component by its node `id` from the `.flow` file.
175	
176	```bash
177	# Add an LLM simulation (non-deterministic, prompt-guided)
178	uip maestro flow eval simulation add <component-id> \
179	  --set "<set_name>" \
180	  --data-point "<data_point_name>" \
181	  --strategy Llm \
182	  --component-type connector \
183	  --simulation-instructions "Pretend to send the email and return success." \
184	  --output-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string"},"messageId":{"type":"string"}}}' \
185	  --path <flow_project> --output json
186	
187	# Add a Static simulation (fixed JSON output)
188	uip maestro flow eval simulation add <component-id> \
189	  --set "<set_name>" \
190	  --data-point "<data_point_name>" \
191	  --strategy Static \
192	  --component-type agent \
193	  --mock-value '{"status":"ok"}' \
194	  --path <flow_project> --output json
195	
196	# List simulations on a data point
197	uip maestro flow eval simulation list \
198	  --set "<set_name>" \
199	  --data-point "<data_point_name>" \
200	  --path <flow_project> --output json
201	
202	# Remove a simulation
203	uip maestro flow eval simulation remove <component-id> \
204	  --set "<set_name>" \
205	  --data-point "<data_point_name>" \
206	  --path <flow_project> --output json
207	```
208	
209	**Strategy selection:**
210	
211	| Strategy | Use when | Key flags |
212	|----------|----------|-----------|
213	| `Llm` | Output should be plausible but non-deterministic | `--simulation-instructions`, `--output-schema` (auto-resolved) |
214	| `Static` | Output must be identical every run | `--mock-value <json>` |
215	
216	For `Llm` simulations, `--output-schema` is **auto-resolved from the `.flow` file** — the CLI reads the node's output definition (connector `outputJsonSchema`, agent `agentOutputVariables`, or `node.outputs`) and injects it automatically. Pass `--output-schema` explicitly only when you need to override the derived schema or the node has no declared outputs.
217	
218	Simulations are stored inline in the data point's `simulations` array within the eval set JSON. Running `simulation add` twice for the same `<component-id>` on the same data point replaces the existing simulation.
219	
220	## Anti-patterns
221	
222	- **Don't hand-write `id` UUIDs on data points.** Use `uip maestro flow eval add` so the CLI generates fresh UUIDs and keeps `evalSetId` consistent with the parent set.
223	- **Don't pass `--inputs` keys that aren't in the flow's input schema.** The CLI rejects unknown keys before writing the data point.
224	- **Don't set `--expected '{}'` and skip `--criteria` for trajectory evaluators.** Both placeholders end up empty; scoring is meaningless.
225	- **Don't delete attached input files before the run completes.** The CLI references them by path until upload to Studio Web finishes.
226	- **Don't expect `--evaluators` on `set add` to auto-update.** Adding new evaluators later does not retroactively link them to existing eval sets.
